newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares close lower on Wall St, growth data.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares close lower on Wall St, growth data.

text.p: Chilean blue chips ended softer with the bolsa pulled lower by Wall Street's slide and fears that the higher-than-expected April growth will delay a further cut in interest rates, said brokers.
The bolsa is seen resuming its downward drift at the opening, they said.
"Tomorrow looks like another soft day. Demand in the U.S. has dried up with space for profit-taking," said one dealer.
The 40-share index closed down 1.06 percent at 131.5 points. The general index shed 0.53 percent to 5,729.58 points amid thin turnover of 8.3 billion pesos.
Chilean American Depositary Receipts closed sharply lower on the back of Wall Street's 2.5 precent tumble -- the second largest daily fall in the Dow's history.
In Santiago, the market reacted coolly to the official Imacec index which showed the economy grew a stong 6.5 percent in April, said brokers.
The figure showed economic growth picked up sharply from March and sparked concerns that the Central Bank will continue with its tight interest rate policy, they said.
The market was dragged down further by news Smith Barney had slashed Chile's weighting in its portfolio to underweight from overweight, citing recent overperformance, said dealers.
"It was a real slap in the face for the bourse after the Imacec data," said one trader.
Losers included steel-maker CAP, down 1.6 percent at 1,230 pesos, power giant Endesa, down 1.32 percent at 307 pesos and paper producer CMPC which shed 1.09 percent at 4,995 pesos.
Gainers included pension fund manager Provida, up 4.6 percent at 9,100 pesos and Banco Edwards which rose 0.94 percent at 53-1/2 pesos.
